# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-16

**Long-form fell to 3,567 views on 2026-11-13, its lowest day in two weeks, and the Ravana long-form due 19 November has no draft on disk. The owner's note changes the Tipu Short: the fall of Srirangapatna and who took the treasure, not the birthday. All three decisions carry forward on the same dates.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish the Ravana fact-check long-form: who first argued that Ravana was the wronged side.** (long, due 2026-11-19, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Long-form fell to 3,567 views on the last day counted, and the three Ravana Shorts hold 74,487, 70,386 and 29,606 views with no long video to send those viewers to. Over the 365-day window a long-form view brings 8.66x the subscribers a Shorts view does. Three days are left.  
   First step: Write the first minute today. Open on the sentence in William Hunter's book of 1882, shown on screen; name him second; stay with him to 0:30. No tour of versions after the opening.
2. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: The owner's note of 15 November sets the story: the prize money and palace treasure taken on 4 May 1799, then the British writing of Tipu as a tyrant. The Karnataka row over his legacy has been in the news since 10 November and nothing is scripted. His birth date is disputed, so the Short rests on the news, not on the birthday.  
   First step: From the prize records and Wellesley's dispatches, choose the one sum or object that shows who got rich, check it against the original, and build sentence one on it.
3. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: It is the top-ranked dated moment of the next three weeks and it sits with Aurangzeb, the subject of the channel's two largest videos. The four biggest videos brought 66.5% of the channel's lifetime subscribers, and this month no video has reached that size: 0 subscribers against 844 planned from such videos.  
   First step: Have the named sources in hand by 17 November, then write sentence one as the order, the place and the date. Tell it as an act of state, not a martyrdom story.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
17,500 subscribers against a target of 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 18,537, which needs 46.2 net a day. The 7-day rate is 51.7, above what the month needs; the 28-day rate is 30. Projection basis: 7-day rate. On that basis the month ends at 18,224, 313 short, and the channel is 344 behind the ramp today. Do not read the 7-day rate as the new normal: upload subscribers peaked between 8 and 11 November, and long-form brought four new subscribers on 13 November against 23 two days earlier. Uploads now account for 56.5% of net subscribers over 28 days, so the older finding that most growth came from outside the videos no longer holds. The lever furthest behind is breakouts: 0 subscribers against 844 targeted this month. 0.61 of a breakout at the median 1,393 subs. The demonstrated route is a newsjack of a mass release (Chhava gave three of four) or an evergreen controversy with a searchable name; check the calendar and news releases for the next peg. Long-form did 78,275 views in the last 7 days of Analytics against 75,701 the week before, but the last day was 3,567. Shorts did 137,727 against 77,035, most of it one Ravana Short on 11 November; their last day was 7,960. Over 28 days long-form earned 69.5% of the net subscribers that uploads brought. Last week five Shorts went up. The two that beat the usual for a Short were both about Ravana. None of the five was something the briefs had recommended, and nothing the briefs recommended was made. That is the case for three decisions, and for putting the Ravana long-form first.

What's working
- The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History” at 12.1 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the shape of the Ravana long-form: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”
- Ravana is what viewers are choosing: “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita: The Scene the Ramayana Movie Skipped” has 74,487 views at 77.2% average view, and “Was Ravana Good or Bad? The Ramayana Movie Controversy Began in 1882” has 29,606.
- The growth now rests on videos. Uploads brought 475 of the channel's 840 net subscribers over 28 days, and long-form brought 330 of those against 145 from Shorts.

What's wrong
- Long-form is running out and nothing is ready to follow it. “Ramayana’s Many Versions” stands at 8,268 views and 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000 a week after release. Probable cause, from its post-mortem: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: in the Ravana long-form the minute after the opening stays with the opening's man; compare the drop at 0:35.
- Reach from the film is not turning into subscribers. “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has dropped to 8.5, out of its usual range, now that one video is 42.3% of long-form views in that window; only 41.2% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of this is the count. Probable cause: every film video answers one scene or tours a map, and none names a culprit. Test: the Ravana long-form on the same traffic; compare per 1,000 on day three.
- The line planned as the long-form's opening already lost viewers once. In “Was Ravana Good or Bad?” 17 points left at 0:06, on the words “1882 when a British administrator called”. Probable cause: a date and a job title before the viewer knows what the man did. The lesson on file: “Opening on a credentials biography loses more viewers than any other open on the channel; start at the moment the evidence appears.” Test: open on what the book says, name the author after, and compare the first 30 seconds.
- “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” did not widen: 1,244 views three days on, under the usual for a Short, though its like rate is 8.8% against a Shorts median of 3.9%. It lost 13 points at 0:05, where the script turns from the question to describing the manuscript. Probable cause: the first five seconds give the feed no person and no quarrel. Test: no second Constitution Short on this pattern.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-13. Long-form is still a Home-feed channel: 142,443 of 158,159 long-form views over 28 days came from the bucket that holds Home and the subscriptions feed, and 3,712 from search. Shorts drew 25.9% of their views from search over the same 28 days; the older finding that search carries the Shorts no longer holds this month.
- The film window is still open. The Ramayana page on English Wikipedia is at 2.91x its 30-day median eleven days after release, and the month's Shorts search terms are still Ravana and Sai Pallavi variants with no long-form behind them.
- Birsa Munda and Nehru lead the Wikipedia spikes, at 17.98x and 23.84x their medians on Hindi Wikipedia. Both are calendar days, 15 and 14 November: attention for a day, not standing demand.
- 20 November is a Friday, the strongest evening in the niche's comment data, where activity peaks between 18:00 and 22:00 IST. Publish the Tipu Short an hour or two before 18:00 IST; the own sample is small, so treat the hour as a test.
- WhatsApp referred 12,380 views over the 365-day window against Instagram's 443; the base is views from outside YouTube, a small part of all views. Send the Ravana long-form out on WhatsApp on day one.

## How they are reacting
Under the Ravana Shorts the argument has settled on motive: the film gives Ravana revenge where the epic gives lust and arrogance. Under the E. V. Ramasamy Short viewers already name the man they blame, which the long-form's second act can use. One viewer has noticed what the numbers show: the film Short gets the comments and the history video does not.
- **The film swapped lust for revenge** (mixed): "Maybe I'm oversimplifying this but the core reason for why he abducted Sita Ji is for lust and arrogance, now in Namit Malhotra's Ramayana they properly showed the arrogance part but replaced lust with revenge which leads to the controversy"
- **Context does not excuse Ravana** (negative): "Kya fark padta h kya context hai??Kidnapping someone’s wife is still a heinous crime"
- **Viewers already blame E. V. Ramasamy** (negative): "He was the guy that sowed the seeds of political poison in TN, the effects of which impact the people even today."
- **The film Short gets the comments, the history video does not** (mixed): "Funny how a video about a movie attracts so many comments and a genuine historical video related to India, to create awareness doesn’t garner much attention"
- **Correction: the Cholas did send a fleet** (mixed): "I have a doubt how about Rajendra chola conquering srivijaya that counts right also Nice vid"

Requested topics
- Rajendra Chola and Srivijaya, as the answer to “never sent a single soldier”
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- The Panchatantra's journey into West Asia

## Competitors
Eleven days after release the watchlist is still on the film. Project SHIVOHAM put up a long-form on the film's hidden details in the last 24 hours and it is the fastest-moving long upload on the list. Verdicts and reactions are taken. Nobody has traced where the sympathetic Ravana came from, with names and dates.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Boycott the Ramayana? What?"
  Why it worked: 103,638 views at 20.7x the channel's median. The first sentence speaks to what the viewer is about to do: “If you plan on boycotting the new Ramayan movie, you might be doing more harm than good”.
  Steal: Start from the viewer's own position and turn it. For the Ravana long-form's title and thumbnail, speak to the viewer who left the cinema liking Ravana.
- **The Emissary**: "Why Did Japan Make Indian Propaganda Posters?"
  Why it worked: 467,162 views at 12.5x. An object is on screen in the first second, “Check out these posters from India's freedom struggle. Japan made them”, and the question follows from it.
  Steal: Open the Tipu Short on one object taken from Srirangapatna and say whose hands it went to.

Gaps
- Where the sympathetic Ravana came from: three own Shorts, the month's search terms, and no long-form from Itiha or anyone on the list.
- “Reality of Aurangzeb” (Mohak Mangal) still has no answer from the record on any tracked channel. The 24 November Short is that answer, told from the sources and never as a reply.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, long, 4/5**: Ramayana film, day 11: the window is still open  
  Signal: Box-office headlines are new again today and the Ramayana page on English Wikipedia is at 2.91x its median. The radar's step for this week is the fact-check long-form. (Moments radar, Wikipedia pageviews, news)  
  Make: This is decision 1. The hour it publishes, pin it under the three Ravana Shorts and both Ramayana long-forms. Judge it on day three, not day one.
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: the next dated moment, no Short scripted  
  Signal: Correction: the radar tags the day as his birth anniversary and yesterday's brief followed it. The owner's note says the birth date is disputed, so neither the title nor the script should claim the birthday. (Moments radar, controversy news, owner's note of 15 November)  
  Make: Decision 2, in dates: script on 16 and 17 November, record on 18, publish by Friday 20 November before 18:00 IST, judge on day three. Name the men who took the treasure in sentence one, and tell the event whole: the film Shorts that answered a single scene brought reach without subscribers.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November: no Short scripted  
  Signal: The top-ranked dated moment on the radar, eight days out; its next step falls on 17 November. The day is a public observance. (Moments radar, calendar)  
  Make: Decision 3, in dates: sources by 17 November, script by 19, record by 21, publish on the evening of 23 November, judge on 26. The lesson on file: “Name the event, not the theme; and do not publish on the festival day itself.”
- **watch, short, 3/5**: 4 December: Bentinck's sati regulation of 1829, with a script already written  
  Signal: On the radar 18 days out; its first step opens on 20 November. The tool lists a Short script on English wife-selling set against sati, written on 17 September and not recorded. Itiha's sati Short of 22 October has 1,719 views, so the subject alone does not carry. (Moments radar, scripts on disk, own Analytics)  
  Make: Not a decision this week. On 20 November reread the script: if sentence one is a dated sale with a price and a place, record it for 3 December; if it opens on an argument, leave it.
- **watch, skip, 2/5**: Constitution Day, 26 November  
  Signal: The day-three check on “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” is in: 1,244 views, under the usual for a Short. (Calendar, own Analytics)  
  Make: Skip the second illustration Short that yesterday's brief held open. The first did not widen and the week is full.
- **watch, skip, 1/5**: Birsa Munda: top of X India and a Wikipedia spike  
  Signal: First on X India for Janjatiya Gaurav Divas, and 17.98x his 30-day median on Hindi Wikipedia. (X trends via getdaytrends, Wikipedia pageviews)  
  Make: Skip. The day was 15 November, and a freedom fighter's life story is the kind of Short the feed has rated lowest on this channel.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [4/5, long] **Who Made Ravana the Wronged Hero? It Began With a British Book in 1882**  
  Decolonization reframe; Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named author convicted from his own page; Contested history  
  source: Decision 1
- [3/5, short] **Tipu Sultan's Death: Who Got Rich From It**  
  Empire and extraction: the prize money and the palace treasure; Contested history: the Karnataka row; Villain plus hypocrisy: the men who took the treasure wrote the verdict on him  
  source: Decision 2. Owner pick of 15 November. Second title on file: “Tipu Sultan Died at This Gate. The British Wrote Everything After”
- [3/5, short] **Aurangzeb's Order, Chandni Chowk, 1675: Why the Ninth Guru Was Executed**  
  Identity and religion stakes; Villain plus hypocrisy: a named emperor and a dated order; Contested history  
  source: Decision 3
- [3/5, short] **Britain Banned Sati in 1829. Englishmen Were Still Selling Their Wives**  
  Villain plus hypocrisy; Decolonization reframe; Identity and religion stakes  
  source: Script on disk since 17 September, for 4 December. The title is this brief's suggestion, not the script's
- [2/5, short] **Did India Really Never Send a Soldier? Rajendra Chola's Fleet**  
  Contested history: the channel's own claim, corrected by its viewers; Identity and nation stakes  
  source: The most-liked correction under the Asia long-form

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,317 followers, up 214 in 7 days. Carousels remain the growth format: median carousel reach is 7,173 against 1,905 for reels. The latest reel, a pointer to the full conversation, has a skip rate of 63.7% against a reel median of 54.2%; a reel that opens on a promotion gives the viewer nothing to stay for. Owner pick of 15 November, for Instagram only: post the “Itihasa vs Myth” clip as a reel, or a recut that opens on who first filed the Ramayana as mythology. It is not among the recent reels yet.

Do more
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 38 followers (91 posts); outside the band, 12 (14 posts). Pooled rate 3.01 vs 1.51 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact.
- Write carousels that revise a received story  
  52 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 22 for the other lanes (39 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 12.5k, conversion 3.85 vs 2.12 per 1k.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  18 of 103 rated posts are shared above the median (26.1/1k) but convert below it (2.2/1k): median 13.1k reach for a median 13 followers. The 34 posts that do both average 283 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen.
- Stop posting single images  
  86 single images all time: 77.1k reach between them and 105 followers, 1.2 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 160. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken.

  The video it points to brings 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000 views since release; the other brings 12.1 in the 90-day window.
- **this_week**: Answer the Chola correction under the Asia long-form and pin the answer.  
  It is the most-liked correction on the channel's largest long-form, and acknowledging Rajendra Chola's fleet costs one comment.
- **this_week**: Check “Itihasa vs Myth” and “Is Caste Unique to India?” in Studio for visibility history and restrictions.  
  They stand at 74 and 247 views two weeks on, with days of zero after publish. Still open from yesterday.
- **later**: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.  
  Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing, so the website is left out today.
